h2. 1. Environment

* *Site:* Production — [https://app.shopview.com] and the customer portal [https://portal.shopview.com]
* *Build:* v26.36.4-3e1c643
* *Organisation:* Bilal-Trucks · *Location:* Truck Hill 1
* *Records used:* invoice *INV-S1-764* ([https://app.shopview.com/workorders/58bfdc33-1f89-4c4a-94c3-e02b3bc843f6/finance]) and estimates *S2-864* and *S2-833*
* *Observed:* 12 September 2026

h2. 2. The problem

Two things look different between the Legacy and the Modern design on the same document. Neither is
a rule breach on the face of the specification — both are asked about here so the Product Manager can
say whether they are intended.

*(a) Per-line fees are grouped differently.* On invoice INV-S1-764 the labour line carries a *Flat Fee
of $12.00* and the parts line a *Percentage processing Fee of $12.00*. Legacy leaves those out of the
per-line subtotals; Modern folds them in.

*(b) A Legacy estimate prints a Payments and Balance block that the Modern estimate does not.*

h2. 3. Steps to reproduce

# Open the invoice for a job that has per-line fees — for example [https://app.shopview.com/workorders/58bfdc33-1f89-4c4a-94c3-e02b3bc843f6/finance] — or open it on the customer portal.
# In *Settings → Invoice*, turn the *"Legacy invoice layout"* switch *on*, confirm, and read the per-line subtotals.
# Turn the switch *off* (Modern), confirm, and read the same subtotals again.
# For (b), view an estimate for a job that has payments recorded against it, under each setting.

h2. 5. Current behaviour

*(a) The per-line block:*

|| || Legacy || Modern ||
| Labour subtotal | {{Labor Total $135.00}} | {{Labor $147.00}} (135 + the 12.00 flat fee) |
| Parts subtotal | {{Parts Total $90.00}} | {{Parts $102.00}} (90 + the 12.00 processing fee) |
| Line total | {{Line Total $225.00}} | {{Line total $249.00}} |

*The summary block below it is identical in both:* {{Labor $135.00}}, {{Parts $90.00}}, then an
Adjustments section carrying the same figures. Modern additionally itemises the two fees there as
{{Labor $12.00}} and {{Parts $12.00}}. *Every grand total on the document is the same in both designs*
— {{$304.94}}, {{$317.39}}, {{$206.39}}, {{$111.00}}, {{$32.00}}, {{$15.00}}, {{$14.94}}, {{$29.88}},
{{$4.98}}, {{$7.47}}. The customer is billed the same amount either way.

*(b) On an estimate*, Legacy prints a Payments and Balance block that Modern omits entirely. On S2-864
that reads {{Payments (Deposit) Sep 9, 2026 - Check $500.00 (Deposit) Sep 9, 2026 - DEBIT CARD of
$600.00 — $348.09 will be credited $251.91 Balance $0.00}}, and on S2-833 {{Payments Balance $149.27}}.
Word counts across the two renders of S2-864: {{Payments}} legacy 1 / modern 0, {{Balance}} legacy 1 /
modern 0, {{Deposit}} legacy 2 / modern 0. The estimate's own figures are identical in both.

h2. 6. Expected behaviour

Unknown — that is the question. Either:

* both are intended, because each design keeps its own way of laying a document out; or
* a customer who receives the same invoice in the two designs should not see a different line total, and
  an estimate should not show payments in one design and not the other.

h2. 7. Sources

The specification permits a layout difference of this kind. Confluence page {{845447188}}, "Invoice
Design Selection — Product Spec", *version 27*, last edited 2026-09-11, read on 12 September 2026:

{quote}S2-R7: A document's figures, totals, line items and numbering are identical in both designs.
Blocks that belong to a design's layout may differ between the two; the remit-to block is the known
case (S2-E3).{quote}

and, naming this behaviour directly:

{quote}Three pre-refresh behaviours are kept for fidelity because they change layout rather than
figures: the remit-to fallback, *the Adjustments grouping*, and the VIN placeholder word (Q7).{quote}

So on the written requirement both observations are compliant: the figures, totals, line items and
numbering do match, and the grouping is a deliberately kept Legacy behaviour. *What the specification
does not say is whether the resulting difference is acceptable to a customer*, which is why this is a
question rather than a defect.
